# Business insights (auto-generated by `python -m mks.cli insights`)

Every number below is computed from the pipeline outputs. Demand = unconstrained demand; forecast = P50.

## 1. Headline

- Next 12 months (Nov-26 to Oct-27): **1.75M units** (+2.7% vs last 12 months, 1.71M) and **$1.56B revenue** (+7.6% vs $1.45B).
- 19-month plan: **2.74M units / $2.47B**.
- Revenue grows faster than units by about 4.8 points: January price rises are in the plan (volume-weighted price effect +5.4% vs last known price).
- Shape & Trajectory Dynamics: Winter 2025-26 was a demand-driven dip (not supply-driven; stockouts were under 0.3% of volume). The forecast returns toward the 2024 level because the model finds no growth driver in the flat macro paths. Mid-2027 to 2028 YoY of -2% to -7% is therefore the least-evidenced part of the plan; use it with the P10-P90 range.

## 3. Seasonality and holidays (plan capacity around them)

- Monthly index (2023-2025 complete years, 1.00 = average): 01: 0.93, 02: 0.92, 03: 1.05, 04: 1.04, 05: 1.06, 06: 0.99, 07: 1.00, 08: 0.92, 09: 1.08, 10: 1.06, 11: 1.02, 12: 0.93.
- Average observed holiday effect on affected region demand: Lunar New Year -32%, Ramadan -8%, plant shutdowns -55%, retooling -40%. These recur in the forecast window and are modelled with a holiday-fraction feature.

## 4. What supply constraints cost

- 5,830 supply-constrained SKU-region-months logged; fill rate 58.7%; **81,827 units / $82.11M of sales never shipped**.
- Lost revenue by reason: Semiconductor allocation $62.02M, Logistics delay $5.58M, Supplier quality hold $5.19M, Capacity constraint $4.71M.
- Lost revenue by family: Electrical Assemblies $64.84M, Thermal Management $4.06M, Powertrain Components $3.44M (top 3).
- The stockout file is incomplete; unlisted months inside the documented semiconductor window were estimated, so real losses are higher than the file shows.

## 5. Risk and procurement

- Portfolio P90 buffer above P50 by family (shrunk toward pooled all-family buffer of 19.8%; small samples): Brake & Safety Systems +15.1% (raw +12.1%, n=38), Chassis & Structural +15.2% (raw +12.3%, n=38), Electrical Assemblies +26.9% (raw +31.4%, n=38), Hydraulic Systems +27.3% (raw +32.0%, n=38), Precision Machined Parts +20.1% (raw +20.3%, n=38), Powertrain Components +15.6% (raw +12.9%, n=38), Thermal Management +16.2% (raw +14.0%, n=38).
- Unhedged SKU-level safety stock buffer by family (leaf quantiles summed): Brake & Safety Systems +46%, Chassis & Structural +46%, Electrical Assemblies +47%, Hydraulic Systems +47%, Powertrain Components +46%, Precision Machined Parts +46%, Thermal Management +44%.
- Key takeaway for planners: Order to P50 at portfolio level; add the ~16% aggregate cover for the family; only apply individual leaf P90 buffers (+44% to +47%) to critical single-source or long lead-time parts to prevent 4x inventory over-ordering.

## 8. Actions for planners

- Review **133** series with a structural level shift (>=2.5x vs the prior 12 months, global movement removed): confirm whether the new level is permanent.
- **16** active-status series have had no demand for 6+ months (possible lost accounts): confirm before committing materials.
- **89** series changed ordering cycle; **23** switched customer. The forecast follows the latest regime.
- Confirm the planned launches' dates and the EOL SKUs' last-time-buy volumes with product management; the forecast uses the predecessor's historical ramp and a learned wind-down.
- EV-062 (Orion Driveline NA retooling, Jul-Aug 2027) is applied as a 78% volume cut for that customer. Replace with the customer's confirmed plan when available.

## 9. Caveats

- Accuracy is by design much better at aggregate than SKU-month level (see docs/VALIDATION_REPORT.md): plan families and regions from the forecast; use SKU-level numbers with the intervals.
- The forecast assumes no supply limits (rule 7); actual shipments will be lower if constraints recur.
- Macro indicators for 2026-11..2028-05 are the file's own forward path; the model uses them only through a few trend features.
